entities.summary: Stasinus of Cyprus was a semi-legendary early Greek poet from Cyprus (Cyprus), born unknown and died 700 BCE. He is best known for his lost work Cypria, which was one of the poems belonging to the Epic Cycle that narrated the War of Troy. Stasinus is also associated with the city of Cyrene (Cyrene), where he may have lived or been active. He is considered one of the poets of the Epic Cycle, which was composed in the 8th century BCE and consists of nine poems that narrate the legendary story of the Trojan War. Stasinus' poetry is thought to have been heavily influenced by the mythology of the Cypriot city of Kition (Kition), where the poet is believed to have been active. The legacy of Stasinus can be seen in the continued influence of the Epic Cycle on Western literature, particularly in the works of Homer and Virgil. Stasinus' poetry has been lost to time, but his influence on the development of Greek poetry is still felt today.
